RESULT [agents]: 51.38% 'exceeds % of humans' on Weco-Kaggle Lite, and above median in 50% of those competitions. With o1-preview it won medals in 16.9% of MLE-bench competitions (vs 4.4% for other agents), and valid submissions rose from 63.6% to 92.4%.
US [agents]: The one-atomic-change rule is the tree-search form of 'controlled small increments'. Change one data source (or one hyperparameter) per round, so that when a round regresses the cause is identifiable. Its plain argmax selection is also the pattern AIRA later showed overfits to noise, so combine it with a hidden gate.
